deviations.description: Re-run the verification bar with no environment override and confirm exit 0.
deviations.reason: REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh exits 1, not 0, due to Rule F (check_deployed_script_drift) firing on the script's own self-reference: the deployed .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh has not been regenerated to match the source-store edits made in this task, so it now differs byte-for-byte from the source copy. This is a known, pre-documented structural gotcha (see .memory/10-Memories/MEM-workflow-check-extension-docs-rules.md's 'Self-reference hazard' section) that is orthogonal to SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE. Regenerating .claude/ via deploy-headless.sh is restricted to skill-orchestrate's own Stage MT-3 redeploy checkpoint (per that script's own header comment), not a general implementation agent, so this implementer cannot resolve the drift itself. Verified instead via targeted checks: (a) grep for 'Rule T:'/'Rule U:' findings in the full run log returns zero matches, (b) all 19 extensions show PASS in the per-extension summary table (only 'core' shows FAIL, solely due to Rule F), (c) the advisory-override run (SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE=advisory) produces the identical single Rule F FAIL and no schema findings either way, proving the override escape hatch and the hard-mode default both behave identically with respect to Rules T/U. This confirms the plan's substantive claim (all extensions pass Rule T/U under hard mode) while leaving the incidental deploy-drift FAIL for the orchestrator's own redeploy step.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — raw exit code is 1 due to an expected Rule F self-reference deploy-drift FAIL, not a SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE/Rule T/U regression; confirmed via targeted grep that zero Rule T/U findings occurred and all 19 extensions PASS — see summary)*
